definitions: James Stephen Ewing (1866–1943) was an American pathologist who was the first to describe a form of bone cancer that was later named Ewing's sarcoma.
Ewing's sarcoma, also known as Ewing sarcoma, is a rare type of cancer that occurs in bones or in the soft tissue around bones. It is named after James Ewing.
examples: James Ewing made significant contributions to oncology.
The discovery of Ewing's sarcoma is attributed to James Ewing.
